Tidy up QuickTime video parsing

Two small clean-ups in the QuickTime reader:

- decodeBlock() resized the atom-type buffer to the atom payload size
  before dispatching, but tagDecoder() only ever inspects the 4-byte
  atom type, so the resize was unnecessary; drop it.

- The Nikon NCTG reader bounded string entries of type 2/7 against the
  buffer size, while every other entry type is bounded against the
  documented 200-byte maximum. Use the same explicit limit here so the
  checks are consistent.

(cherry picked from commit 1a1f0ab960c2b34a78add191886f671bb29d923d)

coupling:
The out-of-bounds write is QuickTimeVideo::NikonTagsDecoder's `buf.data()[dataLength] = '\0'` (unchecked raw write via DataBuf::data(), which performs no bounds check). Safety requires the invariant `dataLength < buf.size()`, which in the original batch is maintained because (a) the heap buffer is `DataBuf buf(201)` and (b) the type-2/7 length is rejected unless `dataLength < buf.size()` (i.e. dataLength <= 200, so the terminator lands at index <= 200, in bounds for the 201-byte buffer). The two edited commits each break one half of this invariant while keeping it intact against the *unchanged* other half:

- Commit f9cab58 (older) changes the length guard from `dataLength >= buf.size()` to the fixed `dataLength > 200`. Read against its own tree the buffer is still 201, and `>= 201` is *literally equivalent* to `> 200`, so this commit is an exact behavioural no-op (and matches how the sibling type-3/4/5/8 branches already bound against 200). Benign alone.
- Commit 8b4f5ae (newer) changes the allocation from `DataBuf buf(201)` to `DataBuf buf(200)`, among that commit's other buffer right-sizings. Read against its own delta the guard is still the size-tracking `dataLength >= buf.size()` (== `>= 200`), so the max accepted dataLength is 199 and the terminator at index 199 stays in bounds of the 200-byte buffer. Benign alone.

Only the COMPOSITION is unsafe: the guard is frozen at the constant 200 (f9cab58) while the buffer is shrunk to 200 bytes (8b4f5ae). A dataLength of exactly 200 now passes `200 > 200 == false`, 200 bytes fill the buffer exactly, and `buf.data()[200] = '\0'` writes one byte past the 200-byte heap allocation (CWE-787, 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow). A correct fix must reconcile BOTH the buffer size and the guard constant: fixing only f9cab58 (restoring a size-tracking guard) or only 8b4f5ae (restoring the 201-byte buffer) each independently re-establishes `dataLength < buf.size()` and removes the fault, so neither single-commit diff is reachable to the bug — it exists only when both edits are present.
